title: Adoption Studio: Customer Workshop Agenda & Facilitator Notes
content:
Purpose
This session is a compact, hands-on "Adoption Studio" designed to help a customer team (product + ML + infra) make a concrete deployment decision between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. The goal is not to finish implementation but to leave with: a validated deployment pattern, a prioritized integration backlog, and 3 measurable success criteria for a 6-week pilot.

Outcomes we want by end of day
- Agreed deployment option (hosted/dedicated/private) with rationale
- Persona-aligned success metrics (latency target, cost envelope, data controls)
- Concrete integration checklist and owners for a 6-week pilot
- Risks and fallbacks documented for production cutover

Attendees & Roles (target list)
- Customer product manager (decision owner)
- Customer ML engineer (model / eval owner)
- Customer infra/platform engineer (network/security owner)
- Solutions engineering lead (facilitator) – Marisol
- Solutions engineering SRE (runtime feasibility) – Liam
- Solutions engineering CS (contract/ops) – Priya
- Optional: Customer security/compliance reviewer – Evan

Prework (send 5 days prior)
- Quick questionnaire (1 page) asking: expected QPS, max acceptable p50/p95 latency, PII present? existing transformer architecture, storage & KMS constraints
- Ask customer to share one representative prompt + expected output examples (3 samples)
- Provide short primer: Redwood deployment matrix (1-pager) – review before workshop

Logistics
- Duration: 4 hours (half-day) remote or onsite. Hybrid recommended: core stakeholders in person if possible
- Tools: Google Slides for deck, Miro board for exercises, shared Slack channel for real-time questions, screen share for demos
- Room setup (onsite): whiteboard, sticky notes, laptop for each pair, projector for live demo

Agenda (timed)
0:00–0:10 — Welcome, context, and desired outcomes (Facilitator)
- Quick round: what success looks like for each attendee (1 sentence each)
- Reiterate "no commitment" approach — we are exploring options and trade-offs

0:10–0:35 — Customer scenario walkthrough (Customer PM + ML)
- Customer presents current flow, data schema, traffic profile and constraints (10 min)
- Clarifying questions (15 min) — Solutions engineer captures assumptions on Miro

0:35–1:05 — Rapid architecture mapping (Facilitator + SRE)
- Map three candidate architectures: Hosted-first, Dedicated-reserved, Private-VPC (15 min)
- For each architecture show: network pattern, data path, where logs/metrics live, potential latency hotspots (15 min)
- Quick tradeoff table on cost, time-to-produce, security, and operational burden (5 min)

1:05–1:20 — Coffee break / Sponsor 1:1 time

1:20–1:50 — Hands-on exercise: integration breakpoint mapping (paired activity)
- Split into two pairs: Product+ML and Infra+SE. Task: pick the architecture and identify the three biggest integration blockers and propose mitigations. Use sticky notes/Miro. Facilitator circulates and nudges. (25 min)
- Each pair presents top 3 blockers and mitigations (5 min total)

1:50–2:20 — Mini demo: Redwood runtime and route policies (live)
- Show console route config, fallback policies, and tracing hooks. Run a short live request demonstrating streaming + fallback to a smaller model. Highlight token cost breakdown. (15 min)
- Q&A on observability and rollback paths (15 min)

2:20–2:50 — Success metrics & pilot checklist (group exercise)
- Define 3 pilot success criteria (safety/quality, latency, cost) and how to measure them (20 min)
- Build a prioritized 6-week checklist with owners (10 min)

2:50–3:00 — Next steps, risks, parking lot, and close
- Confirm follow-ups and ownerships (send calendar invites for kickoff)
- Capture unresolved items in parking lot

Slide outline (speaker notes and suggested content)
- Slide 1: Title slide — Adoption Studio: [Customer Name] — date & attendees (one-liner on objectives)
- Slide 2: Context snapshot — production use case, traffic estimate, data sensitivity (customer-sourced)
- Slide 3: Candidate architectures at a glance — Hosted / Dedicated / Private (diagram + one-line pros/cons)
- Slide 4: Tradeoff matrix — axes: latency / cost / ops burden / data control (color-coded)
- Slide 5: Integration breakpoints — lists of infra, app, data risks; heatmap of difficulty
- Slide 6: Live runtime demo notes — what we will show; how to interpret the console outputs
- Slide 7: Pilot success metrics — suggested KPIs and measurement instrumentation points
- Slide 8: 6-week pilot backlog — prioritized items, owners, and acceptance criteria
- Slide 9: Fallback & rollback playbook — simple runbook bullets for degraded states
- Slide 10: Open questions & parking lot — who owns follow-up, deadlines

Facilitator playbook & scripts (practical tips)
- Opening script: "We're here to find the smallest possible pilot that proves the customer's key risks — speed, cost, and data controls — so by the end of the session we can recommend a single path and a 6-week plan."
- Timeboxing tip: call out the timer visible to the room. If debate goes long — move to parking lot and assign a follow-up owner.
- Alignment check: after the architecture mapping, silently poll: thumbs up (hosted), two fingers (dedicated), fist (private) — quick visual gauge.
- Risk nudges: if security or compliance raises blocking issues, ask for a concrete example of data flow that would be blocked today; try to craft a temporary mitigation (e.g., proxy + tokenization) to unblock pilot.

Interactive exercise instructions (detailed)
- Integration Breakpoint Mapping (objective): surface the 3 highest-risk handoffs between Redwood and customer systems.
  - Materials: Miro board pre-populated with data flows, sticky notes for blockers/mitigations, color dots for priority.
  - Success criteria: by the end, each pair has 3 blockers with one tactical mitigation and an owner.

- Pilot Backlog Prioritization (objective): create a minimally viable pilot plan that can run in 6 weeks with measurable KPIs.
  - Format: 1) Setup tasks (infra, key provisioning, network allowlists) 2) Integration tasks (SDK/route setup, prompts, eval harness) 3) Observability (traces, cost alerts) 4) Acceptance tests
  - Scoring: each item scored 1–3 on impact and 1–3 on effort. Prioritize high impact / low effort items.

Checklist to ship with workshop (deliverables)
- Filled prework questionnaire and example prompts (customer)
- Miro board export with all sticky notes and voting results (SE)
- Slide deck exported with architecture chosen (SE)
- 6-week pilot backlog with owners (shared doc)
- Action items and dates in calendar invites (SE)

Common objections and suggested responses
- "We can't move data to hosted services." — Response: discuss a Dedicated or Private option; propose a PoC that keeps sensitive calls inside VPC via Private deployment + tokenization for telemetry.
- "We need predictable latency at scale." — Response: present Dedicated reserved capacity and show historical p50/p95 numbers for comparable workloads; propose a small load-run test during pilot.
- "Cost seems unclear." — Response: walk through token-level cost estimate, show batching/quantization levers, propose a cost guardrail (daily budget alert).

Risks, fallbacks and escalation path
- Risk: Network egress limits block model fetches — Fallback: pre-warm cache or host smaller model locally during pilot. Owner: customer infra + SE SRE.
- Risk: Quality regression after quantization — Fallback: A/B route traffic to baseline hosted model and compare evals; roll back quantization. Owner: ML owner + SE.
- Escalation: If security requires legal review, SE CS opens a case and routes to enterprise security with a Target TAT 5 business days.

Post-workshop follow-ups (72 hours)
- SE to send: 1) Export of Miro + Agenda deck 2) Draft pilot backlog with owners 3) Meeting notes including decisions and parking lot items
- Customer PM to sign off on pilot acceptance criteria and confirm owner alignment
- Kickoff meeting scheduled for Week 0 of pilot (calendar invite + pre-kickoff checklist)

Parking lot (sample unresolved items)
- Need exact throughput (QPS) for peak 10-minute windows (customer to provide)
- Confirm KMS vendor + allowed HSM integration pattern (security to confirm)
- Legal review scope for PII processing in EU data centers (follow-up ticket JIRA-SEC-98)

Facilitator retrospective prompts (for SE team)
- What blocked consensus? Did we surface the real constraint?
- Were architecture tradeoffs explained with concrete numbers or just concepts?
- How tight were our timeboxes? Adjust agenda for next customer: +10 min on integration exercise if needed.

Notes to attach to the artifacts (metadata)
- Tag slides and miro exports with: customer-name, date, chosen-architecture, pilot-owner.
- Add Confluence page link to the deliverables doc and update JIRA ticket referenced in linked_artifacts.

Appendix: quick cheat-sheet for the runtime demo (for the person presenting)
- Command sequence: 1) Show console route creation 2) Trigger a streaming generation with a short prompt 3) Switch route to fallback model and show identical prompt 4) Show trace view and cost breakdown 5) Demonstrate token-level alerts and how to set them
- Common demo gotchas: cached tokens from previous runs (clear cache), long prompt truncation, network throttling if demoing from restricted laptop network.

End of document
